clue.text: Responsible for cards arriving late

parts.note: to be behind something is to be responsible for it
the cards a player holds are a hand

explanation.surface: Someone is blamed for the greetings cards turning up after the birthday.
explanation.definitionFit: Behindhand means behind schedule, overdue, which is a synonym of late.

clue.text: Record India's poetry for programme

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record
India is I in the phonetic alphabet; the 's adds S
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: An Indian poetry recording is being made for a broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: An episode is a single instalment of a serial, one broadcast programme.

clue.text: News of independent country taking shape

parts.note: I is the abbreviation for independent

indicators.note: one word taking another takes it in, so the second sits within the first

parts.note: a nation is a country
form means shape

explanation.surface: Reports about a newly independent state coming into being.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking shape' reads as an idiom for developing, but it splits: the country takes in the shape just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Information is facts that have been told or learned, which is what news consists of.

clue.text: Clergyman sliced with iron during golf, so blasted

indicators.note: a word sliced open with something has that thing pushed into the cut

parts.note: a dean is a senior clergyman
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
in means during, as in 'in the war'
G is golf in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A vicar hacks his shot with an iron on the course and swears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sliced', 'iron' and 'golf' all suggest a bad shot on the course, but iron is the metal and golf is a letter of the phonetic alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound so loudly blasted out that it overwhelms the ears is deafening.

clue.text: Father child at work with mate, shocking director

indicators.note: letters at work are busy being put to a new use, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
cock is a British friendly form of address, like mate

explanation.surface: A dad brings his child to work and pals up with a colleague, which seems scandalous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shocking' looks like a comment on the scene but belongs to the definition: Hitchcock made shockers like Psycho.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Hitchcock was the film director famed for suspense and shocks, the master of the thriller.

clue.text: Good to interrupt dreadful sad song

indicators.note: something that interrupts breaks into the middle, so it is placed inside

parts.note: dire means dreadful
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A cheery note breaks into an awful, mournful tune.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirge is a lament for the dead, a mournful piece of music.

clue.text: Knight on foot is slow man

parts.note: a paw is an animal's foot
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A mounted knight dismounts and walks, so moves slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' places the knight's letter after the foot in this across entry; chess pieces are 'men', and the pawn moves only one square at a time.
explanation.definitionFit: The pawn is the chess piece that moves just one square per turn, the slowest man on the board.

clue.text: Director giving secretary a lift home

indicators.note: in a down entry, giving someone a lift raises them to sit on top of the other piece

parts.note: a PA is a personal assistant, a secretary
D is the abbreviation for director

explanation.surface: A boss drives his assistant home after work.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, giving the secretary 'a lift' puts PA above the director's letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Pad is informal slang for the place where someone lives.

clue.text: Shelving unit that now wobbles

indicators.note: a wobbling thing is unsteady, so the letters are shaken into another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A rickety bookcase has started to wobble.
explanation.definitionFit: A whatnot is a stand with open shelves for displaying ornaments, a piece of furniture.

clue.text: Trash that Wossy would call table tennis?

indicators.note: how someone would call a word is how they pronounce it, so we go by sound

parts.note: wiff-waff is a slang name for table tennis; broadcaster Jonathan Ross, nicknamed Wossy, says R as W

explanation.surface: A wry question about what a TV host would call ping-pong.
explanation.walkthrough: Jonathan Ross is a British TV presenter whose R sounds like W; saying RIFF-RAFF he would produce wiff-waff, an old name for ping-pong.
explanation.definitionFit: Riff-raff means disreputable or worthless people, the rabble, which is what 'trash' means when said of people.

clue.text: Screw back for black again, perhaps

indicators.note: back means the word is read from its end towards its start

parts.note: screw is British prison slang for a warder

explanation.surface: Snooker advice: put backspin on the cue ball to pot the black once more.
explanation.walkthrough: Screw-back is a snooker shot, but 'screw' is a prison guard. Blacking in a sketch with ink is one way to draw it again, hence 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: To redraw is to draw again, and going over lines in black is an example of that.

clue.text: Soap dish on Ben's side

definitions.meaning: first meaning: short name for Coronation Street, the long-running British TV soap opera
second meaning: a bowl-shaped hollow on the flank of a Scottish mountain, a ben

explanation.surface: A soap dish sits beside Ben's bath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soap dish' reads as one bathroom object, but it splits; a ben is a Scottish mountain peak.
explanation.definitionFit: Corrie is the nickname of Coronation Street and also a Scottish word for a cirque, a mountain hollow.

clue.text: Close behind them, improving

indicators.note: behind says the first piece named follows the second in this across entry

parts.note: 'em is the informal shortening of them
a close is an ending

explanation.surface: Following right behind other runners, someone gets better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind them' puts the close's word after 'em in this across entry; 'Close' looks like an adverb meaning near.
explanation.definitionFit: Emending a text means correcting it, so making it better.

clue.text: Simple Hindu arranged flowers

indicators.note: things arranged are put into a fresh order, as with blooms in a vase

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A modest Hindu worshipper arranges flowers as an offering.
explanation.definitionFit: Delphiniums are tall garden plants with spikes of blue blossom, a kind of flower.

clue.text: Great answer, possibly brilliant in retrospect

indicators.note: retrospect looks back, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for answer
a brilliant is a cut diamond, so possibly a gem

explanation.surface: Looking back, a great answer was maybe a stroke of genius.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brilliant' looks like an adjective, but it is the noun for a diamond cut, an example of a gem.
explanation.definitionFit: Mega is informal slang for great or enormous.

clue.text: Old Arab's one quiet mother, very classy

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
sh is a call for quiet
ma is an informal word for mother
elite means of the highest class

explanation.surface: An ancient Arab ancestor is described as one quiet, very refined mother.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Ishmaelites were the descendants of Ishmael, traditionally regarded as forebears of the Arab peoples.

clue.text: Habit back for good, in a manner of speaking

parts.note: an advert is a backing for a product, a good on sale
diction is a way of speaking, of enunciating

explanation.surface: A habit returned for good, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a manner of speaking' looks like the stock phrase meaning 'so to speak', but it holds the wordplay; the advert reading of 'back for good' is a loose cryptic hint.
explanation.definitionFit: An addiction is a compulsive dependency, a habit in the sense of a drug habit.

clue.text: Ref that is not allowed out in different colours

parts.note: VAR is the video assistant referee in football
i.e. is the abbreviation for 'that is'
gated is a British term for confined to college or home as punishment

explanation.surface: A referee is barred from going out wearing a mismatched kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' looks like a sign to rearrange letters, but it belongs with 'not allowed' as part of being gated.
explanation.definitionFit: Variegated means marked with patches or streaks of several hues.

clue.text: Inexplicable sight of a famous restaurant literally empty

parts.note: taken as written
Noma in Copenhagen is a world-famous restaurant

indicators.note: an emptied word has its insides removed, so only its first and last letters survive

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A famous restaurant stands literally empty, a puzzling sight.
explanation.definitionFit: An anomaly is something that deviates from the norm and defies explanation, a strange thing seen.

clue.text: Sulk finishes in which you eff off

indicators.note: the finishes of words are their final letters, so only those are taken

parts.note: the final letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: A sulk that ends with someone storming off swearing.
explanation.definitionFit: A huff is a fit of petty annoyance, a period of sulking.

clue.text: E.g. 5D shortly clutching big white telephone, befuddled

indicators.note: something clutching another holds it in its grip, so wraps around it

parts.note: Fred is a short form of the director's first name, Alfred
the big white telephone is slang for a toilet when one is being sick into it

explanation.surface: A drunk Alfred Hitchcock hugs the toilet bowl, completely confused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Talking on the big white telephone' is drinkers' slang for vomiting into a toilet; LOO is the British word for toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Floored can mean baffled or confounded, completely unable to respond, which is befuddled.

clue.text: Excellent returning on grass, hard court likewise

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the words are read from the end

parts.note: taken as written
grass and pot are both slang for cannabis

indicators.note: likewise says the next pair gets the same backwards treatment as the first

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A tennis player is excellent coming back on grass and on hard courts too.
explanation.walkthrough: Grass and hard court are tennis surfaces, but grass here is cannabis.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-notch is an informal word for first-rate, of the highest quality.

clue.text: Beat from start to finish of Beethoven's first

parts.note: thro is a short spelling of through, meaning from start to finish

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the opening letter of the composer's name

explanation.surface: A rhythm runs right through Beethoven's First Symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: Beethoven's First reads as the symphony; 'from start to finish' looks like it describes a piece, but it gives the poetic shortening of through.
explanation.definitionFit: A throb is a strong regular pulse, a beat.

clue.text: This protected by Asdic on voyage?

definitions.text: This protected by Asdic on voyage?

indicators.note: something protected by words is held inside them, so look within the letters

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and through the next two

explanation.surface: A riddle about what a ship's sonar guarded at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Asdic was the early British sonar used by escort ships to detect U-boats hunting merchant ships in the Second World War; the whole clue defines while the answer sits in its last three words.
explanation.definitionFit: A convoy is a group of merchant ships sailing together under naval escort, which Asdic-equipped warships protected.

clue.text: Women change, becoming male

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for women
alter means change

explanation.surface: A gender transition from woman to man.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: Walter is an example of a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Walter is a traditional boy's first name, so it refers to a male.

clue.text: Match level, wanting run at the end

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so a letter is taken away
at the end says the removed letter is the final one of the word

parts.note: a tier is a level, as in a tiered cake
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A game ends all square because a final run never came.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match level' reads like a drawn game, but 'level' is the wordplay; 'at the end' says which letter goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie is a sporting fixture, especially a cup match, as in 'third-round tie'.

clue.text: Report of a good innings, remarkable one with your bat

indicators.note: something remarkable is out of the ordinary, so the letters leave their ordinary order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cricket write-up praises a batsman's fine knock.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'good innings' is a British idiom for a long life, borrowed from cricket, where an innings is a turn at batting.
explanation.definitionFit: An obituary is a published account of someone's life after their death, the report on a long life.

clue.text: Sound of exhaust, one of four on Lambo?

indicators.note: the sound of a word is how it is spoken, so a word said the same way is wanted

parts.note: to exhaust someone is to tire them

explanation.surface: The roar from a Lamborghini's exhaust pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exhaust' looks like a car part, but it is the verb; TYRE is the British spelling of tire.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lamborghini, Lambo for short, runs on four wheels, each fitted with a tyre.

clue.text: Overdose in graduate college, top grade white powder

indicators.note: in places the first item inside the string formed by what follows

parts.note: a BA is a Bachelor of Arts graduate
King's is a Cambridge college
OD is the abbreviation for overdose
A is the highest mark

explanation.surface: A drug overdose at a university, involving high-grade cocaine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'White powder' suggests a drug, but it is a kitchen raising agent; OD goes between the college and the grade.
explanation.definitionFit: Baking soda, sodium bicarbonate, is a fine white powder used in cooking.
